title: Prove a follow-up after a released boot-recovery binding binds lazily with child-shaped authority
outcome: tm-cr0i releases the stale binding of a finished delegation child at boot (routing_token=None, rebind_required=false). The docs promise that a later follow-up then binds lazily at admission like a never-used session, with child-shaped authority. The release leaves the child in exactly the never-bound shape the existing child-admission tests cover, so tm-cr0i pins only the state transition. Add an explicit end-to-end test (delegation_followup_admission or engram_boot_recovery_targets): finish a child, boot once so its binding is released, then follow it up (rearm_terminal_delegation_for_followup_locked / dispatch_turn_with_followup) and assert a fresh session_bind with external_ref termal:delegation:<id> and no session_status against a stale token. Raised by Claude /review-code on tm-cr0i round 2.
